title: Craniotomy for acute monitoring of pial vessels in the rodent brain
author: Aboghazleh, Alkahmous, et al.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and shave
steps.instruction: Place the rat in an induction chamber with 3 % isoflurane until loss of toe‑pinch withdrawal (≈3–5 min); then shave the top of the head with an electric shaver, starting between the eyes and moving toward the neck.

steps.title: Clean head and verify sedation
steps.instruction: Blow the head with an air canister and wipe with distilled water to remove residual fur; check pedal reflex with a firm toe pinch and, if withdrawal occurs, return the animal to the induction chamber until the reflex is absent.

steps.title: Transfer to stage and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Prepare the microscope stage, transfer the rat, and maintain deep anesthesia with 1.5–2 % isoflurane (oxygen flow 0.8–1 L/min). Continuously monitor breathing: decrease isoflurane if the animal gasps heavily, increase if the animal moves. Ensure the nose cone does not press on the nose tip.

steps.title: Mount rat in stereotaxic frame
steps.instruction: Secure the animal in a stereotaxic frame using ear bars inserted into the external auditory meatus (bone) – start with the outer bar then the bar closest to you – avoiding placement against neck muscle.

steps.title: Set up physiological monitoring
steps.instruction: Continuously monitor blood‑oxygen saturation (SpO₂) with a paw‑clip attached to an animal oximeter pod (ML325, ADInstruments) and a PowerLab (PL3508, ADInstruments); maintain core body temperature at 37.3 ± 0.2 °C using an electrical or water‑jacketed heating pad (insert rectal probe and tape to tail).

steps.title: Adjust lighting and lubricate eyes
steps.instruction: Adjust the microscope light source as needed and apply synthomycine (or any suitable ocular lubricant) to the animal’s eyes.

steps.title: Inject local anesthetic
steps.instruction: ≈10 min before incision, inject 0.3 mL of 10 % lidocaine (diluted to 1 mL with normal saline) subcutaneously into the scalp, distributing the injection over the planned incision area.

steps.title: Disinfect scalp
steps.instruction: Apply povidone‑iodine scrub to the skin for 1 min, then wipe with 90 % alcohol; repeat the scrub‑wipe cycle twice.

steps.title: Check anesthesia throughout surgery
steps.instruction: Before the incision and every 15 min thereafter, test the pedal reflex; if any withdrawal response is observed, wait 10 min and retest. If the reflex persists, increase isoflurane (e.g., from 1.5 % to 2 %) and re‑check.

steps.title: Make midsagittal scalp incision
steps.instruction: Using a size‑3 scalpel handle with a #10 surgical blade, cut a midsagittal incision ≈2.5 cm long to expose the skull.

steps.title: Retract incision edges
steps.instruction: Flip the incision edges to the right and left sides and secure them with tissue clips or surgical thread attached to the corners of the stereotaxic frame.

steps.title: Remove adipose tissue and periosteum
steps.instruction: Excise adipose tissue with small scissors; then, using a surgical blade, draw a circular cut to remove the periosteum and expose the superior skull surface, cutting medial to the temporalis muscle to avoid its fibers. Wash the exposed bone with normal saline.

steps.title: Control minor bleeding
steps.instruction: Apply cautery and cotton swabs to stop any minor bleedings; bone wax may be used if needed.

steps.title: Select cranial‑window size and location
steps.instruction: Choose the diameter and position of the cranial window according to experimental goals; the parietal bone is recommended for easy access.

steps.title: Drill cranial window
steps.instruction: Using a 0.7 mm micro‑drill bit, drill under a surgical/intravital microscope with appropriate magnification. Frequently irrigate the skull with chilled ACSF (or saline) delivered via syringe to keep the bone wet and prevent heat injury; drill slowly and support the hand to avoid pressure on the site.

substeps.instruction: Etch the window borders with the micro‑drill and use this template to guide drilling, alternating sides to avoid prolonged heat on one area.
Continue drilling until the dura is reached or the central bone piece becomes loose.

steps.title: Remove bone flap and manage bleeding
steps.instruction: Lift the loose central bone piece with small toothed forceps; if minor bleeding occurs, rinse the dura with ACSF and apply small cotton balls for a few minutes without pressure.

steps.title: Expose brain – dura‑intact technique
steps.instruction: Using a fine needle (insulin syringe tip or 24‑gauge cannula) with a micro‑hook bent on the tip, gently scratch a shallow longitudinal groove in the outer dura layer from medial to lateral; grasp the outer layer edges with fine forceps and peel them slowly to the right and left, leaving the inner transparent dura intact.

steps.title: Expose brain – dura‑rupture technique
steps.instruction: Select a site free of underlying pial vessels, puncture the dura with the needle to create a small gap, then cut the dura with small forceps or a micro‑incisor. Continuously perfuse the exposed brain with artificial cerebrospinal fluid at 1.0 mL/min.

steps.title: Perfuse brain with ACSF
steps.instruction: Maintain continuous nourishment of the exposed brain surface by delivering artificial cerebrospinal fluid at a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min throughout the imaging session.
